How much does HVAC replacement cost?

Swapping the whole heating and cooling system — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$5,000–$11,000

National average $8,000

Bay Area: $18,500–$26,000 — roughly double the national average, the steepest regional premium we track.

Why quotes run $5,000 to $30,000

System type
Furnace + AC: $7,000–$13,000. Heat pump: $8,000–$16,000. Geothermal: $15,000–$30,000.
Efficiency tier
Variable-speed and high-SEER2 equipment adds $2,000–$4,500. You pay more now and less every month.
Ductwork
Reusing existing ducts keeps the bill down. Full duct replacement runs $7,000–$16,000 on its own.
Electrical
Older panels and new 240V circuits add electrical work. Heat pumps and high-efficiency systems are the hungriest.
System choice

Furnace vs. heat pump

Furnace + AC
$7,000–$13,000

The familiar split setup: gas furnace for heat, condenser for cooling. Cheapest where gas is cheap and winters actually bite.

Heat pump
$8,000–$16,000

One box heats and cools. Higher upfront, lower running costs. Handles Bay Area winters without breaking a sweat.

Bottom line: in the Bay Area’s mild climate, the heat pump is usually the better buy. Furnace + AC still wins where gas is cheap and it truly freezes.

Common questions

How long does installation take?

One day for a straight equipment swap. Two to four days with new ductwork, electrical upgrades, or permits in the mix.

How long do HVAC systems last?

Fifteen to twenty years for furnaces and air conditioners; heat pumps run about the same with regular maintenance.

Should I repair or replace?

Replace at 15+ years, when repairs come every season, or when jumping efficiency tiers. Repair when the system is under 10 and the fix is minor — a capacitor, a contactor, a thermostat.

Heat pump or furnace?

Bay Area: heat pump, almost always — winters are mild and one box does both jobs. Cold climates with cheap gas still favor the furnace.

Every home prices differently.
